Several mechanisms explain why high-welfare states have avoided the predicted growth penalties. Moreover, efficient tax structures and the stabilization benefits of social insurance can offset potential negative incentive effects.
Rather than viewing social spending and economic growth as fundamentally incompatible, policymakers should recognize that welfare states and dynamic economies can coexist—and that certain social investments may actively contribute to long-term prosperity.
